sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's fromMaybe function, which provides a default when a value is absent — and the type system enforcing you must choose what fills the emptiness
sketches.resonance: When you reach for someone who might not be there, you must decide in advance what absence feels like.
sketches.draft:
missing :: Maybe a
missing = Nothing

whatYouFeel :: a -> Maybe a -> a
whatYouFeel = fromMaybe

-- whatYouFeel default missing

sketches.mechanism: Erlang's process linking: when two processes are linked, if one dies, the other receives an exit signal and dies too — unless it explicitly traps exits
sketches.resonance: Two lives bound together so that one ending destroys the other, unless you deliberately learn to survive loss.
sketches.draft:
-module(together).
-export([us/0]).

us() ->
    You = spawn(fun() -> receive after infinity -> ok end end),
    link(You),
    exit(You, gone).

sketches.mechanism: Ruby's frozen string: calling .freeze on a string makes it permanently immutable — any attempt to modify it raises a RuntimeError
sketches.resonance: Some memories refuse to be rewritten; touching them only causes pain.
sketches.draft:
class Memory
  def initialize
    @last = Object.new.freeze
  end

  def revise
    @last << Object.new
  rescue RuntimeError
    self
  end
end
